clue.text: "Don't get up yet," Sinbad ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so the letters of yet and Sinbad are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Sinbad the sailor tells someone to remain lying down a while longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yet' looks like part of the quoted request, but it joins Sinbad as anagram fodder; 'ordered' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone not to rise yet is urging them to remain lying under the covers.

clue.text: Did butterfly possibly start to pollute wetland?

parts.note: butterfly is a swimming stroke, so doing it is one way of having swum: past tense SWAM

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of pollute is taken

explanation.surface: A question about whether an insect's flight began to foul a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butterfly' suggests the insect, but here it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsh or bog is a wetland, low ground saturated with water.

clue.text: It's sweet that a fight gets under control

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do in practice
something brought under control has been tamed, made TAME

explanation.surface: A cosy claim that bringing a quarrel to heel is a pleasant thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The artificial sweetener used in diet drinks is a sweet substance, a noun sense of sweet.

clue.text: Not enough in a sample of dust to match with

indicators.note: a sample of something is a small taste, here just the first letter of dust

parts.note: to equate one thing with another is to match them

explanation.surface: A forensic complaint that a speck of dust is too little to make a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insufficient or lacking falls short of what is needed: not enough.

clue.text: Carpets are best beaten

indicators.note: beaten means knocked about, so the letters of are best are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Household advice that rugs come cleanest when thumped on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpets' looks like floor coverings, but as a verb to carpet someone is to scold them.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to reprimand them, so the verb means scolds harshly.

clue.text: Pet left annoying American

parts.note: a dog is a typical pet
having left is to have gone

explanation.surface: A household pet has gone off, irritating someone from the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annoying American' reads as a person but is an adjective: the US mild curse word, as in 'that blasted dog'.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang this word is a mild oath meaning damned or confounded, i.e. vexing.

clue.text: Talked for a day with German agreement

parts.note: ja is German for yes
Wed is the abbreviation for Wednesday, a day of the week

explanation.surface: Someone chatted for a whole day with a German who kept agreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: To jaw is informal for chattering at length, so the past tense means chatted.

clue.text: Ballet move from the fifth plane

parts.note: a jet is a type of aeroplane
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A dance step taken from the fifth position, or from some aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifth' suggests the fifth ballet position, but it supplies the fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A jump from one foot to the other in classical dance is a ballet step.

clue.text: What 28 did with rubbish ultimately futile

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of futile

explanation.surface: A judgement that the author's efforts were pointless trash in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is the novelist Steinbeck, whose job was to write.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelist like John Steinbeck put words on paper; his past activity was authoring books.

clue.text: Reveals record, comes second?

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
in a two-way contest, coming second means losing

explanation.surface: A question whether an album that came runner-up is being unveiled.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to make known or uncover, a synonym of reveal.

clue.text: A mountain area in France

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
ha is the hectare, the metric area unit used in France

explanation.surface: A description of a lofty region of the French Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like an article but is the definition: the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter A is spoken by this codeword.

clue.text: Arranging is tougher for singing brothers

definitions.note: the definition is the word that comes before Brothers in the name of the singing duo

indicators.note: arranging puts things in a new order, here the letters of is tougher

explanation.surface: Musical arrangement proves harder for a pair of singing siblings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Righteous Brothers were a 1960s American singing duo; the answer is the word that precedes 'Brothers' in their name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Righteous Brothers, famed for You've Lost That Lovin' Feelin', used this adjective as their group name.

clue.text: A homeless virus possibly the ideal

parts.note: a means per, as in two pounds a head

indicators.note: homeless says the short word for at home is removed from the virus word

parts.note: a virus causes an infection

explanation.surface: A virus with no host might just be the model germ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'homeless' removes IN (at home) from INFECTION, leaving FECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawlessness, the state of being perfect, is the ideal one strives for.

clue.text: Diligence essential to NZ's expansion

indicators.note: something essential to a thing is its core, so only the central letters of the expanded name are kept

parts.note: NZ written out in full is New Zealand

explanation.surface: A claim that hard work drove New Zealand's growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expansion' suggests economic growth but means NZ spelt out in full; 'essential to' keeps its central four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager enthusiasm and devoted effort, keenness, is close to diligence.

clue.text: Definitely compel downfall — about time!

parts.note: to force is to compel

indicators.note: about means around, so the rain word wraps round the time letter

parts.note: rain is a downfall from the sky

explanation.surface: An insistence that a regime's collapse must surely be forced, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downfall' suggests ruin, but it is a fall of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is so without doubt means saying it surely, beyond question.

clue.text: Vegetable hit back in strip cartoon

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable

indicators.note: back means the word for hit is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to stun is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A vegetable lands a blow in a comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Schulz's comic strip starring Charlie Brown and Snoopy carries this title.

clue.text: Let me pour liquid mineral

indicators.note: liquid means fluid, so the letters of let me pour flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone offers to pour out a liquid mineral water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid mineral' looks like a single drink description, but 'liquid' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude oil is classed as a mineral resource, extracted from rock like ores.

clue.text: Self-absorbed characters in El Salvador find lead!

indicators.note: in tells us the words for lead are placed inside the country abbreviation

parts.note: ES is El Salvador's international vehicle registration code
to lead is to go first, written GO 1ST with 1 as I

explanation.surface: Some vain people in Central America strike lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the metal, but means go first, spelt GO 1ST with the numeral as the letter I. 'find' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: People wholly concerned with themselves are self-centred and vain, so self-absorbed people.

clue.text: Town put together around square

indicators.note: around means the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: to stage a show is to put it together
two people who are square are even, owing nothing

explanation.surface: A town assembled round its central square.
explanation.walkthrough: STEVENAGE is a new town in Hertfordshire, north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenage is a Hertfordshire town, England's first post-war new town.

clue.text: Handled Irish politician keeping engineers worried

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the politician's letters go round the rest

parts.note: a TD (Teachta Dala) is a member of the Irish parliament
RE is the Royal Engineers
ate, as in what's eating you, means worried

explanation.surface: An Irish politician dealt with engineers who were fretting.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal with something or someone is to treat it, so handled is the past tense.

clue.text: Policeman stops Europeans being snappy dressers

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the officer's letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: Danes are Europeans from Denmark
a DI is a detective inspector

explanation.surface: A police officer halts some well-dressed Europeans.
explanation.definitionFit: Fops and dandies are men who dress smartly and fashionably: snappy dressers.

clue.text: We stick around, which fielding sides want

indicators.note: around means scattered about, so the letters of we stick are moved round

explanation.surface: Batters vow to stay at the crease, which the opposing team hope to prevent.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielding team's aim is to take wickets, i.e. dismiss batters.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the side in the field tries to dismiss batters; each dismissal is a wicket taken.

clue.text: Debate extremes of weather with fish

indicators.note: extremes of means the outermost letters of weather

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod

explanation.surface: Arguing about harsh weather while out fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue or dispute at length is to haggle and squabble, i.e. debate.

clue.text: A number caught inside in the past

indicators.note: inside means the letter for caught is placed within the number

parts.note: one is a number
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Some batter was caught a while back.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly, at some earlier time, as in once upon a time.

clue.text: Chasubles, perhaps for 100 primates

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
apes are primates

explanation.surface: Church vestments, perhaps destined for a hundred monkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasuble is a sleeveless priest's vestment, a kind of cloak, so an example of this garment.

clue.text: Injustice fires a nun's storm

indicators.note: a storm whips things up, so the letters of fires a nun's are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A wrong done enrages a nun so much that she rages.
explanation.definitionFit: Injustice is the quality of not being just or even-handed; a synonym.

clue.text: Glossy small vegetable

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a leek is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A shiny little vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth and shining, as of a well-groomed coat of hair.

clue.text: Star newspaper to read

parts.note: the i is a British newspaper
to con is an old word for studying or reading carefully

explanation.surface: A celebrity wants a newspaper to read.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British daily paper (a spin-off of The Independent).
explanation.definitionFit: A famous celebrity, someone idolised, is an idol or star.

clue.text: Former setter finally getting pregnant

parts.note: ex means former
pectin is the agent that makes jam set

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of getting

explanation.surface: An ex-crossword compiler is at last expecting a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' suggests a puzzle compiler but is the gelling agent in jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with child is said to be awaiting a baby, a common euphemism.

clue.text: Jewel, one of 19?

parts.note: a means one
the answer to 19 across can mean a small gate, as in a wicket gate

explanation.surface: A gem, perhaps one of the cricket stumps' prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: A wicket is also a small gate, so one of them is A GATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious stone, used as a gem.

clue.text: Perry maybe with plum as one ingredient

indicators.note: an ingredient is a part of a mixture, so the letters are part of plum as one

explanation.surface: Perry, the pear drink, perhaps made with plum as an ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perry' suggests the pear cider, but is Perry Mason, the TV lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Perry Mason is Erle Stanley Gardner's fictional lawyer, so Perry is an example.

clue.text: Author could make 10 be sick

indicators.note: could make means the letters might be reworked into another word

parts.note: 10 is ten

explanation.surface: An author whose book is enough to make ten people ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 here is the number ten, not the answer to 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck wrote The Grapes of Wrath, so he is an author.
